newsitem.title: EU: EP DEBATES SUPPLEMENTARY BUDGET REQUIREMENTS FOR 1997.
newsitem.headline: EP DEBATES SUPPLEMENTARY BUDGET REQUIREMENTS FOR 1997.

text.p: EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT SESSION NEWS PRESS RELEASE

Tuesday, 15 July - Discussions concerning the supplementary Budget requirements for 1997 and the 'Ad hoc Procedure ' for the Preliminary Draft Budget for 1998 were treated together. Laurens Brinkhorst (Nl, ELDR) for the Budget's Committee on the Supplementary and amending Budget for 1997, opened the debate by pointing out that initially the Commission's request was for the creation of 107 new posts to act on the undertakings it had given to augment DG XXIV and to improve its' control systems. However, given the fact that real recruitment possibilities during the 1997 budgetary exercise were, according to the Commission's own estimates, no greater than 35, the budget committee considered that this was the number of new posts that should be created immediately whilst rationalisation and redeployment of staff should be used to further reinforce the sectors concerned, and this new approach to staffing policy was approved by Detlev Samland (D, PES). Mr Brinkhorst's report calls on the Commission to further reinforce the EU's anti-fraud body UCLAF in order to carry out fraud prevention checks, however the new posts required would have to be found within the Commission's existing programme.

Michael Tappin (Staffordshire West and Congleton, PES) emphasised the undoubted need to reinforce the Consumer Health Policy Unit which had been made only too clear by the problems raised by the BSE crisis and now by the outbreak of swine fever.

Regarding the request by the Court of Auditors for increasing its establishment plan by 23 posts the budget's committee proposes that the Court initially receives 16 new posts directly related to auditing and two new posts for the Administration. Juan Fabra Vallis (E, EPP) pointed out that whilst budgetary austerity was necessary this could not be to the detriment of the efficiency and cost effectiveness of the Institutions. The request of the Court was undoubtedly justified in view of its increased workload. He pointed out that it was the only Institution which had effectively achieved 0% growth in its establishment plan in the past.

All speakers agreed that the 'Ad Hoc Procedure' for the 1998 budget, which enables Parliament to participate in the definition of the actual amounts of compulsory expenditure, was a success, and that cooperation between the budget's committee and the agricultural committee, had been greatly enhanced. Jan Mulder (Nl, ELDR), draftsman for the agricultural committee recommended adoption of the Commission proposal and that growth in agricultural spending should be limited to 0.45%. However, a difference of approach between the Council and Parliament remained. Whereas the Council preferred a linear approach to cuts in expenditure, Parliament favoured specific cuts. The cuts should be based on proposals by the Commission in a letter of amendment which should be submitted as late as possible, in order to ensure the most up to date data. Joe McCartin (Connacht/Ulster, EPP) pointed out that in his opinion the costs of enlargement could not be financed by mere savings or shavings from agriculture. Real resources would be necessary in both agricultural policy and structural policy if new member countries were not to be disappointed and existing member states were not to feel frustration. He called for a Marshall Plan approach to this problem. Jim Nicholson (Northern Ireland, I-EN) followed on the same lines. He considered that whilst farmers could expect financial difficulties and he was against the reduction of farmer's incomes, however, penny pinching was not the answer and fraud needed to be stamped out. He then pointed to the severe losses incurred by beef farmers in the United Kingdom and said that measures to promote agriculture and regain consumer confidence needed more resources.

In concluding the debate Commissioner Erkki Liikanen again approved the effectiveness of the ' Ad Hoc Procedure'. He stated that he would be looking at the fisheries agreements with Commissioner Bonino in the near future.
